name: Remacera

items.name: Destined Renewal
items.text: A remacera is permanently affected by their own curse of renewal. When a remacera dies, after 1 minute, their new body appears 1d20 miles from where they died. They can also choose to retain their current form.

items.name: Curse of Renewal
items.text: A creature damaged by a remacera's jaws must succeed at a DC 24 Will save save or be afflicted with the curse of renewal. A creature that dies while affected by this curse is subjected to the effects of a successful Reincarnate ritual that takes effect after 1 minute, regardless of whether the soul is willing to return.

items.name: Murderous Rhapsody
items.text: hen a creature the remacera reduced to 0 Hit Points dies, the remacera gains 10 temporary Hit Points that last for 1 minute and is Quickened for as long as they have these temporary Hit Points. They can use the extra action only to Stride or Strike.

items.name: New Growth
items.text:
The remacera spawns tiny, larval remaceras within a creature they can see within 100 feet. That creature must attempt a DC 24 Fortitude save save.

---
Critical Success The creature is unaffected.

Success The creature becomes Clumsy 1 for 1 round as some larvae spawn on its skin before harmlessly falling off.

Failure As success, and the creature is Sickened 2 as several larvae burrow out of its skin.

Critical Failure As failure, but the creature is Sickened 3 and Off-Guard while it remains sickened.

items.name: Ultrasonic Ululation
items.text:
Frequency once per round

Requirements The remacera has a creature Grabbed or Restrained in their jaws

---
Effect The creature takes 2d10+8 sonic damage with a DC 24 basic Fortitude save save. A creature that fails is also Stupefied 1 for 1 round (1 minute on a critical failure).

text:
Remaceras are mysterious fey who represent the natural cycle of transformative rebirth and metamorphosis. They believe that the cycle of reincarnation is the greatest expression of rebirth and revel in opportunities to send other creatures down this path. To a remacera, acts of violence are akin to scavengers and bacteria helping dead organisms decompose—and there may be some truth to this, as it isn't uncommon to find strange blossoms and fruits in their wake.

Remaceras take the form of enormous caterpillars with striking patterns and serene human faces. Their calm visages are shattered when they stretch their jaws unnaturally wide to reveal a mouthful of deadly, sharklike teeth, which vibrate at high frequencies to damage and disorient foes. The most ancient remaceras can grow as long as 13 feet and weigh thousands of pounds.

Despite their violent proclivities, remaceras savor the opportunity to have profound conversations with intelligent creatures. They seldom hold those who slay them in contempt, for they too receive renewal in death. Those who undergo a crisis of belief and turn nihilistic return as escorites.
